title: Open measurement protocol for ride accelerations (bystander/seat-mounted data logging)
context: RideBelt is an open, safety-critical Hee-Lee Oss project: an optional rider-worn backup restraint (low hip belt + short tethers; optional clip-on Shoulder Module or one-piece Integrated Harness) that latches into an open seat anchor standard (RAS). ALL safety content is DRAFT and not for use until a credentialed engineer signs off at the MVP gate (GOVERNANCE.md). Never remove a DRAFT banner, never give instructions for wearing or attaching anything to a ride, never copy text from paid standards (cite by number and title only), never name private individuals or incident victims, and respect the patent design-arounds in docs/research/patentability-fto.md. Physics-education programs routinely measure ride accelerations with phones and data loggers. A consistent protocol would make future open data comparable. Depends on: ridebelt-accel-002 (do those first or use their outputs if merged).
objective: Write a measurement protocol: sensor choice, sampling, axis conventions, calibration, metadata, data format matching accel-002, and park-rule compliance (only with park permission; never attach anything to the ride or restraint).
acceptanceCriteria: States clearly: only with the park's permission and within park rules; no device attached to the ride, seat or restraint
Axis and units conventions match data/accel schema
